name: hits
character: How a cue accents the picture: which sound lands on a cut and which on a movement, how many accents a minute, and whether an accent is dead on or delayed by the audience's reaction time.

dead_on.why: an explosion or a cut needs no processing: dead on the frame (ITU-R BT.1359)

reaction.why: a line or a look needs the audience to absorb it first; the accent follows the reaction time

motion.note: music-to-motion synchrony is detected inside a 300-450 ms window, narrowing to about 150-200 ms as tempo rises

density.note: hitting every cut is Mickey Mousing; the ratio caps what share of adjacent cut pairs may both be hit

sources: https://www.itu.int/dms_pubrec/itu-r/rec/bt/R-REC-BT.1359-0-199802-S!!PDF-E.pdf (A/V sync: +45 ms early to -125 ms late)
https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2015.00736/full (synchrony window narrows at faster tempi: about 200 ms at 60 BPM, 150 ms at 120 BPM)

provenance.classes.reaction.after_s: starting value: 350 ms sits inside the 300-450 ms synchrony window
